decisions.executionNote: Raise the left arm through an elbow-up approach toward the rear-left tube; begin aligning to its diagonal axis, keeping the right arm parked.
Approach above the rear-left tube while rotating the open left gripper toward a top-down grasp aligned with the cap-to-tip direction.
Finish top-down alignment and move slowly toward the rear-left tube; use the next wrist view to refine centering before closing.
Refine the rear-left tube grasp using its wrist-image offset: shift toward the cap, correct diagonal yaw, and lower gently with the gripper open.
Correct the wrist-observed tube tilt about the vertical axis, then close around the centered tube body. Retention will be checked during a short lift.
Lift the first tube clear with the left gripper kept closed, checking that its position remains fixed between the fingers before transport.
The tube remains centered after lifting. Begin turning it upright while carrying it toward the rack's left-front large slot, staying above the rack.
Complete the upright orientation over the left side of the rack, maintaining the closed grasp and clearance for visual slot alignment.
Lower the upright first tube toward the left-front slot with a closed grip, pausing above full depth to verify alignment from the wrist view.
Make a small rightward slot-centering correction and continue a slow vertical insertion of the first tube; keep the grasp closed until seated.
Seat the first tube a little deeper and open the left gripper while keeping it still; verify upright support before withdrawing.
The first tube appears upright in the slot. Withdraw the open left gripper while raising the right arm in its own workspace to approach the second tube.
Continue the right-arm elbow-up approach and diagonal grasp alignment. Move the open left arm back toward its home region, clear of the seated tube.
Finish returning the left arm while bringing the right gripper down above the remaining right-side tube. Keep the right gripper open for wrist-based centering.
Refine the right tube's wrist alignment: correct the small diagonal tilt and shift toward its body as the open gripper descends. Left arm settles at home.
Make the final small right-tube centering and yaw corrections, lower to grasp height, and close the right gripper. The next lift will test retention visually.
Lift the second tube clear of the table with the right gripper held closed; verify it stays between the fingers before turning toward the rack.
The second tube remains retained. Begin turning it upright and carrying it above the rack's right-front slot, with the left arm parked.
Complete the upright turn and approach above the right-front rack slot, preserving clearance and the closed right-hand grasp.
Lower the second tube upright toward the right-front slot, keeping the gripper closed and stopping short of full depth for visual alignment.
Apply a small inward and rearward correction to the second tube while descending slowly into the right-front slot; keep the grasp closed for the depth check.
Seat the second tube to the remaining depth, then open the right gripper without translating. Check that the rack supports it upright before retreating.
Withdraw the open right gripper from the seated second tube while raising the left arm for the final tube. Keep both arms in their own workspaces and elbow-up.
Approach the final left-side tube from above while rotating toward its cap direction. Continue retracting the open right arm toward home, away from the rack.
Complete the left gripper's top-down turn above the last tube and lower to a pregrasp height. Bring the open right arm closer to its origin without crossing workspaces.
Use the left wrist view to straighten and center the last tube while lowering partway to grasp height. Finish the right arm's gradual return to origin.
Make the final small lateral and yaw correction to the last tube, lower to grasp height, then close the left gripper. The right arm remains at origin.
Lift the last tube clear while keeping the left gripper closed. Check retention before carrying it to the remaining rack slot.
The last tube remains retained after the lift. Start its upright turn and carry it toward the unoccupied middle-front rack slot, above the two seated tubes.
Continue turning the retained final tube upright while moving above the middle-front slot. Keep its tip clear of the two already seated tubes.
Finish the upright orientation and lower the final tube toward the middle slot, with a small rightward correction based on the head view. Keep the grasp closed for alignment.
Center the final tube between the two seated tubes and descend slowly into the middle-front slot. Keep the left gripper closed until the final depth check.
The last descent shows contact and tube motion in the fingers. Unload slightly, correct the middle-slot alignment a few millimeters left and back, then retry gently rather than pushing further.
Release the final tube without further downward pressure, then lift the open fingers slightly to inspect whether it settles into the slot or needs a higher regrasp.
The released tube has settled lower. Withdraw the open left gripper upward and back to clear the rack and inspect all three tubes without further contact.
All three tubes now appear upright and released in the rack. Retract the left arm toward origin through the raised elbow-up path, keeping both grippers open.
